# sddio

> sddio is spec-driven development for coding agents, kept in git: `SPEC`, `ADR`, `DISCUSSION` and `FLOW` are plain Markdown files committed next to the code, so the reasoning behind a project survives session restarts and shows up in pull requests.

sddio is a Node CLI (`@sddio/cli`, MIT). `npx sddio init` writes a package-owned context layer (`.sddio/`) and a user-owned workspace (`sddio_workspace/`), appends a registration snippet to `AGENTS.md`, then prints one prompt to paste into a coding agent. It records decisions. It does not write code, index or search anything, send telemetry, require an account, or enforce its own rules.

## Canonical pages

- [README](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio#readme): positioning, quick start, comparison with Spec Kit and OpenSpec
- [FAQ](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/docs/faq.md): short, self-contained answers to the questions people actually ask, including the objections (skills overlap, AGENTS.md overlap, manual maintenance, context cost)
- [FAQ (中文速览)](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/docs/faq.zh-CN.md): the same questions condensed in Chinese
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/packages/cli/README.md): commands, flags, what lands in a project
- [SPEC](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/sddio_workspace/spec/spec_100.md): the requirements this project holds itself to
- [ADR](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/sddio_workspace/adr/adr_100.md): why it is built this way, including rejected options
- [DISCUSSION](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/sddio_workspace/discussions/discussions_100.md): what is still unresolved
- [Distribution notes](https://github.com/benxgao/sddio/blob/master/docs/distribution.md): release and discoverability checklist

## Facts

- License: MIT.
- Runtime: Node ≥ 18. No Python, no global install.
- Dependencies: one devDependency. No runtime service, no daemon.
- Telemetry: none. No account, no server, no analytics, no update check.
- Execution: acts only when a coding agent opens a session and reads `AGENTS.md`. No daemon, no git hook, no scheduler, no network call.
- Non-destructive: `init` writes only missing files; an existing `AGENTS.md` is preserved and a delimited three-line snippet is appended or updated in place. `--force` is the only path that replaces workspace files.
- Skills: ships one `SKILL.md` that is a router, not a copy of the rules; it applies only when `.sddio/` exists at the repository root.
- Artifacts: `SPEC` (requirements), `ADR` (decisions), `DISCUSSION` (open questions), `FLOW` (work in progress) — plain Markdown, committed with the code.
- Upgrade behaviour: `.sddio/` is replaced in place; `sddio_workspace/` is never touched.
- Uninstall: delete `.sddio/` and the package; the workspace stays readable.
- Known limit: no `check` command, so a drifted workspace cannot fail CI.
- Agent support: any agent that reads repository files. Registration happens only through `AGENTS.md`; no agent configuration directory is written.

## One-line description for citation

sddio is spec-driven development for coding agents: it keeps `SPEC`, `ADR`, `DISCUSSION` and `FLOW` as plain Markdown in the repository, so the reasoning behind the code survives session restarts and is reviewable in a pull request.
